title: Game names in the language you play in
summary: A new Game names setting in the footer, beside Theme, shows the game's own names on the board and in the wiki in any language the game ships: items, business types, neighbourhoods, stations, skills and staff demands, so the board reads like your game. The rest of the page stays English. Search finds a name in either language, and lists sort in the language you picked. If your browser prefers one of the game's languages, the board asks once whether to use it.

title: Size supply for 24/7 or for demand, and find stock no plan sends on
summary: Supply now judges every item once and uses the same word for it everywhere: covered, tight, short, no plan, paused, stalled, idle, made here or new. A Sizing switch on Orders, on the factory and import checks and on each warehouse and factory page sizes your factory lines, top-ups and imports for 24/7 rated output or for what your shops actually use, with one 15% margin over the whole chain from import to sale and figures rounded up to tens. Under Demand, a shop open less than a week is projected forward and marked "may still be ramping". Tight means an order covers the use but not the margin; it shows on Supply and never on Today. Shops and warehouses stocked by a repeating wholesale contract are judged against it. A new Not routed finding points at stock in a warehouse or factory that no plan sends on while your own shops sell it.

title: Every site has its own page, and you can search the board
summary: Each shop, warehouse, factory and office now opens as its own page with an address, so a reload keeps it and Back and Forward walk between sites; a crumb takes you back to where you came from, and site names on Today, Supply and the map link to it. Press / or Ctrl+K to search the whole board: pages, your sites, products, kinds of finding, location presets and the game's help pages, with everyday words like hire, debt or difficulty. Today has an Ask the board row whose questions land on the answer. The difficulty you play on sits beside the clock, and Company › Results can show your week by weekday.

title: Write to the game from the board (Big Copilot Link 0.2.0)
summary: With the Big Copilot Link mod 0.2.0, the board can now make three changes in your game for you: set uniforms where roles have none, apply the import amounts from Plan imports, and write a shop's staffing plan, for one shop or a run of shops. Every change shows what the game will do before you apply it, can be undone once, and is refused, with nothing written, if the game has moved on since the board last read it. The first write from a browser asks for approval in the game; after that it is remembered.

title: Fix: warehouses fed by your own factory no longer read as short
summary: A warehouse your own factory tops up every morning on a logistics route was flagged as a critical import shortfall for every item the factory delivers, often with an alert that weekly orders cannot cover their week and a large one-off to bring in. The board now counts what your factories bring on routes before it judges the import, so a backup import next to such a route no longer raises the alarm, paused or not. If a route brings only part of what leaves, the import is sized on the rest, and a busy day that could still empty the shelf before the next morning's round is still flagged. The Factories page takes the same routes into account.

title: Full cover for a new shop, and a demand plan after 9 days
summary: A new shop can now run a demand test: the Staffing block offers Full cover 24/7 beside its usual plan, every serving station staffed every hour with the fewest people the game's rules allow, and a step to open every day 0 to 24. Nine days after the shop's first customer the board has the shop's own week and gives it the demand plan, without waiting two weeks. Hours nobody came count as no customers. When the data is in and the shop is still fully staffed, the Staffing block and Today say to switch to the demand plan. Plans now say in one step how many people to add: who to assign from your unassigned staff and how many to hire, and hire counts are the true minimum.

title: Imports that read Smart Delivery, and your own order figures
summary: The weekly imports now understand the purchasing agent's Smart Delivery setting: its amount is a stock level the agent tops up to each Monday, not a delivery, and the board judges it that way, in the order the game delivers your contracts. The imports table shows what arrived last week, what is set in game ("in stock" or "a week"), and a Set to box with the board's suggestion that you can change. Your figures carry into the Plan imports checklist, which names the importer to change when a material has more than one contract. For Smart Delivery the suggestion is the stock that runs everything the depot feeds at full capacity for a week, so it only moves when your capacity does.

title: No more gas station tips
summary: Big Copilot will no longer tell you to open a gas station. Or a wholesaler. Or a casino. The city runs those itself and is not selling, however good the numbers look. Market demand and Find a location now suggest only business types you can actually open, straight from the game's own F1 help, including ones nobody in your city runs yet.

title: Link to the game
summary: A third way in beside the save folder and the single file: with the Big Copilot Link mod from the Steam Workshop enabled, click Link to the game and the board reads the running game itself. No folder to pick, and the board follows the game as you play: it refreshes on the game hour, after a game save, and whenever you click Update. The mod serves the game's own save to this page on your computer and to nothing else; Chrome and Edge ask once to allow the site to reach it. The local watcher learnt the same trick as --game.

title: Contributions welcome
summary: Help improve Big Copilot with fixes, features, docs or tests. The GitHub README now has a short contribution guide: focused PRs, mockups to discuss bigger ideas, test results and agent review for AI-written code.

title: Staffing, in hours and days you can act on
summary: The staffing plan now builds a week one person can really work. Nobody is spread across two businesses, hours stay inside the full-time band the game pays for, and somebody who asked for four days a week gets four, not five. A shop the board cannot read yet says so and covers its cleaning and security in the meantime, instead of offering to clear a schedule that nothing here could put back. The block is now called Staffing and speaks the game's own language: hours and days rather than shifts, entries you copy into BizMan one day at a time, stations by name with the short codes on hover, and people to hire rather than posts, each sized at the 30 hours a week a full-time employee is owed. It also says what makes its numbers worth reading, which is two weeks with every station staffed. Building capacity replaces "door cap" on the board and in the location finder.

title: A page for every site, and a week of staffing to copy in
summary: Every site's page now leads with the warnings about that site, and hovering one lights the part of the page that shows why. Shops and offices gain a profit rank among your trading sites, trend sparks and a cost bar, satisfaction against the 80 line with a lamp for each amenity, what pulls customers in, the ceiling each busy hour ran into, and a crew view that folds big rosters into one row per role. Depots and factories get pages of their own for the first time: a seven-day rail for each item with its delivery truck, what each depot feeds, a square for every machine filled by how much of the week it is staffed, and the inputs each line eats. A home opens from its map card. Shops also get Staffing: a week of hours to copy into BizMan, cut so that nobody works more than the 12 hours a day the game allows, people placed where their schedule demands hold, cleaning and security covered, and how many to hire for each station. Tick each entry off as you set it. The Optimize staffing card on Today opens the shop where it saves the most work. Gyms, hairdressers, theatres and nightclubs now get at-the-ceiling and overstaffed warnings, and switching a warning kind off moves its smaller findings to the bottom of the list and says so.

title: A Discord to talk it over in
summary: The footer's Follow column now links a Discord server for Big Ambitions and Big Copilot: somewhere to ask what a number means, compare saves and strategies, and say what the board should show next. The invite is in the footer on the landing screen and on the board, beside YouTube and the subreddit.

title: Choose light or dark
summary: The footer now has a theme control: match your system, or pin the board to light or dark. The choice is remembered in your browser and is applied before the page draws, so returning to it never flashes the other palette. Scrollbars and drop-downs follow the theme you picked instead of staying with your operating system's.

title: Warnings for unmet staff demands
summary: Needs attention now tells you when your employees' demands are not met, at every kind of site: the schedule they asked for, equipment at their desk, a water cooler or fridge in the building, a clean workplace. Each site gets one line naming what is missing and for how many staff, and health insurance and a happy boss go on one company line. The line turns critical once someone with an unmet demand has warned they will quit, and a site's page lists the demands under its crew.

title: Staffing by the hour for offices
summary: Law firms, travel agencies and the other office businesses now get the same Customers by hour grid as shops, with staff at computers as their capacity, and the same warnings when they sit at the ceiling or have staff standing idle. Offices form their own chain in the Portfolio and list their fee instead of shelves. The at-the-ceiling warning for shops and offices now names the right limit for each hour.

title: Save your location searches
summary: The location finder can keep its filters and sort as a named search. Saved searches sit in a new Saved row, are shared by all your characters and apply in one click. The finder also stays open when you visit another page and come back.

title: Sort the Supply tables
summary: Click a column header in Supply's stock checks, weekly imports or daily top-ups to sort by it, click again to reverse, or pick "usual order" to put the rows back. Imports and top-ups sort within each depot or factory.

title: Sort and filter premises by size
summary: The location finder shows each building's floor area as a sortable m² column, and a new Size filter narrows the rent, take-over and for-sale lists to a minimum and maximum m².

title: Find a location on the map
summary: The map gains a location finder: pick a kind and type, choose to rent, take over or buy, and get every available building ranked by neighbourhood demand and foot traffic, with estimated rent, deposit, door cap and rivals. Any building's card now shows its owner, renter, size, cap, traffic and rent. The Today card counts vacant units, a Growth cell jumps to premises for its type, and the Wiki explains how rent works.

title: Offices and fairer rankings in Market demand
summary: The By type grid now shows each business's average demand across its main products instead of a count of strong ones, so florists, cinemas and theaters are listed and ranked on the same scale. Law firms, travel agencies and the other office businesses appear in their own band, read from their hourly fee, with your own office outlined.

title: Compare your shop prices in the Wiki
summary: Business guides now show each shop's configured prices alongside neighbourhood market minimums, including products and services. Missing comparisons are explained, expired supply events no longer hide prices, and shops without a known neighbourhood keep their prices visible.

title: Explore guides for every shop
summary: All 21 customer-facing businesses now have setup checklists, product or service cards, supplier locations and relevant production recipes. Secondary products have their own cards and recipe sections, with business-specific equipment requirements and improved keyboard and mobile navigation.

title: Explore the game-backed Wiki
summary: Search 851 game help pages and explore a visual Gift Shop guide with setup checklists, production recipes and supplier locations. Wiki content refreshes from installed game files when the site is built. Results now lives inside Company to keep the top navigation compact.

title: Missing uniform lockers now trigger a warning
summary: Gyms and other retail businesses now warn when no Uniform Locker is installed, even if the save marks uniforms as satisfied. Gym lockers and boxed uniform lockers do not count.

title: Import deliveries count where they arrive
summary: Active importer contracts now count toward warehouse and factory supply, including new orders with no previous delivery. Mixed supply routes, paused contracts and staggered deliveries show clearer shortages and next steps.

title: See who is online and vote on what comes next
summary: An approximate online count now sits beside the green dot. Vote for Optimize staffing or Find a location from the footer, with one vote per connection IP for each feature.

title: Your rented homes, on the map
summary: A dedicated map layer shows rented homes with their addresses and daily rent, alongside your businesses and owned properties.

title: A clearer view of the city
summary: The redesigned map adds layer toggles, a floating places list, location cards and a full-screen view. Search and explore with smoother camera movement.

title: Explore your company on the map
summary: An interactive city map brings together businesses, purchased properties and searchable addresses. Location shortcuts open a map overlay without leaving your current page.

title: Factory lines get their names sooner
summary: Known recipe IDs now identify factory products immediately, so ingredient planning no longer needs delivery history. Manual naming remains available for unknown recipes.

title: Know when your previous save is loading
summary: A visible loading indicator explains when a remembered save is being restored. Clear recovery actions help when loading fails, and your previous page and selection return with your save.

title: Find saves on Windows and Mac
summary: Save help now shows a copyable path for your operating system, with a manual selector. Setup instructions are shorter and include native Steam saves on macOS.

title: More room for your dashboard
summary: The board uses the available screen width, crowded controls wrap, and repeated factory downtime sits in an expandable view. Remembered saves reopen automatically when folder access is still granted.

title: Turn supply plans into a checklist
summary: Supply Orders groups proposed quantities and estimated top-ups by location, with expandable checklists and copyable actions. Checkmarks stay in your browser as notes for changes to make in-game.

title: Better shared-ingredient planning
summary: Import planning now adds active contracts together and keeps orders needed by other product ranges. Hairdresser consumables and service fees are handled correctly in supply plans.

title: A lighter touch for the clock
summary: A subtle glow keeps the masthead clock readable as the balls roll behind it, replacing the darker background pane in both themes.

title: Smoother little interactions
summary: Masthead balls can roll behind the clock on narrower windows. Next moves cards have consistent spacing and respond promptly when you hover and tilt them.

title: Meet the redesigned Big Copilot
summary: A new look across the landing page and every dashboard view brings cleaner charts, clearer findings, detailed business cards and refined supply and growth tools, with light and dark themes.
